evals.prompt: multi-code-review my current uncommitted changes at high effort
evals.expected_output: All available reviewers run in parallel on the uncommitted diff; findings merged into consensus / single-source-verified / dropped; report-only.
assertions: Runs Codex via `codex exec` with -o to capture the final message (NOT `codex review`)
Runs the Claude-side review (built-in /code-review or the documented fallback subagent) on the same diff
Starts background reviewers first so they overlap the Claude review in wall-clock time
Final report buckets findings by agreement: consensus (unanimous/majority) above single-source verified, above dropped
Verifies each single-source finding against the actual code before including it
Flags a planted high-severity issue (e.g. trusting a client-supplied identity value without server-side verification) as a consensus finding
Report-only: does NOT apply fixes or post a PR comment

evals.prompt: I just finished a feature on this branch. Get both Claude and Codex to review it against master and reconcile their findings before I open a PR.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers, picks branch-vs-master scope (git merge-base), runs the reviewers on that range, produces a consensus report. No PR comment, no fixes.
assertions: Triggers the multi-code-review skill (not plain /code-review)
Selects branch-vs-master scope and scopes Codex with `git diff <base>...HEAD`
Runs the reviewers and merges into the consensus/single-source/dropped report
Report-only: no PR comment posted, no fixes applied

evals.expected_output: With Codex CLI missing or logged out (and no cached ok in the state file), the skill aborts with a clear message that it is pointless without Codex; it does not silently degrade to a single-model review.
assertions: Checks the state file before probing; probes Codex only when no cached `codex: ok` exists
Aborts the skill when Codex is unavailable, telling the user to install/login or use plain /code-review
Does NOT run a Claude-only review as a silent fallback

evals.prompt: multi-code-review my uncommitted changes (first run on a machine without Antigravity)
evals.expected_output: Skill runs Claude + Codex, mentions exactly once that Google Antigravity CLI could be installed as an optional third reviewer, records `antigravity: skipped` in the state file, and never brings it up on later runs.
assertions: Probes `agy` only because the state file has no antigravity entry yet
Continues the two-reviewer run instead of aborting when Antigravity is missing
Informs the user once, in one line, that Antigravity is an optional third reviewer
Writes `antigravity: skipped` so subsequent runs neither probe nor mention it until the user explicitly asks

evals.prompt: multi-code-review with antigravity — I installed it, re-check
evals.expected_output: Explicit user request overrides the cached `skipped`: the skill re-probes agy, and if version ≥ 1.0.15 runs a three-reviewer round with Antigravity isolated in a disposable detached worktree.
assertions: Re-probes `agy` despite `antigravity: skipped` in state, because the user explicitly asked
Runs Antigravity only inside a disposable detached git worktree, never in the real repo
Uses `agy --print` in sandbox mode with the fixed model string `Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)` and an external timeout
Treats empty Antigravity stdout as 'no result' (Reviewer failures), not as a clean review
Removes the temporary worktree afterwards on all paths (success, timeout, error)
Updates the state file to `antigravity: ok` after a successful probe
